articles.title: Rupee falls 7 paise to 95.68 against US dollar in early trade
articles.description: In early trading, the rupee slipped by seven paise, settling at 95.68 against the US dollar. Factors such as soaring crude oil prices and heightened demand for dollars pressured the currency. Forex analysts noted that Brent crude's price hovering around USD 91 per barrel has led to a surge in dollar demand linked to oil.

articles.title: Stock markets decline in early trade as crude oil jumps to USD 91 per barrel
articles.description: Market benchmark indices Sensex and Nifty declined in early trade on Tuesday as elevated crude oil prices and rising tensions in West Asia weighed heavily on investors’ sentiment.

articles.title: Indian bonds wobble on oil strain, RBI swap pullback
articles.description: On Tuesday morning, Indian government bonds faced a downturn as oil prices spiked beyond ninety dollars. Concerns escalated after the central bank prematurely ended a diaspora deposit scheme, leading to uncertainty in the market. This pullback in liquidity support has rendered bonds susceptible to changes in oil prices and international rates. The five-year note saw a significant yield rise recently.

articles.title: Trump's approval rating sinks to presidency low of 33% as Iran war drags on
articles.description: Poll finds just 1 in 5 Americans think conflict has been worth it, while 80% expect prolonged US involvement, as war and high gas prices weigh on voters

articles.title: Hormuz Tensions: Reshaping Global Oil Trade
articles.description: The ongoing conflict between the U.S. and Iran is reshaping the global oil market, with disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz leading to stabilized oil prices around $90 a barrel. Diplomatic efforts have stalled, causing significant economic strain and altering trade routes, potentially impacting oil prices into the next year.

articles.description: A jump in oil prices sends jitters through stock and bond markets, keeping investors on edge as the ceasefire between the U.S. and Iran expires.

articles.description: Oil prices rose today as prospects receded for a deal to end the Middle East war, with Iran saying it would adopt a more offensive stance and the United States ruling out extension of a ceasefire deal, heightening worries about energy supply.

articles.description: The expiration of the US-Iran truce has driven oil prices higher and government bond yields upward, as fears of renewed conflict and energy supply disruptions unsettle investors.
